niche: a fine-chemicals plant's calendar 2026 VOC record for its permitted process vent unit, conformed from two batch-system exports across a mid-year cutover, a vent calculation basis kept in two unit systems and the oxidizer's one-minute compliance log, where six reactors, two fluid-bed dryers and a solvent still vent through one closed-vent header to a single regenerative thermal oxidizer
answer: EU-P1 over its 2026 VOC limit: 3.2 tons against 2.5, over by 0.7 tons
analyst_test: With every export conformed and every permit condition read, the easy route takes each batch step's vent VOC from the vent calculation basis, applies the oxidizer's tested destruction to every pound vented while it was on line and counts the offline minutes uncontrolled, and files the unit under its 2026 limit; but in the minutes when the dryers' drying cycles and a reactor's charging exhaust coincide the header carries more than the oxidizer's fan can draw, the excess lifts the header relief to atmosphere untreated, and the unit went over.
domain_test: A batch-process VOC inventory worked the way an air permit engineer works it, each step's vent emissions from the vent calculation basis times one minus capture times destruction, where a closed-vent system captures every pound only while its control device can draw every vent at once; with another field's nouns there is no vent stream carrying solvent vapour, no destruction applied to the share the fan draws and no relief releasing the header's mixed gas, so nothing would decide how much of each pound left untreated.

spine.entity: one executed step of one batch on one vented unit

driver: Several sources discharge through one shared device whose intake is capped, and their discharges coincide only in some intervals, so in those intervals the share above the cap passes untreated through a relief; applying the device's tested removal to everything the sources discharged while it ran misses that share, which only the sources' concurrent schedules set against the cap reveal.
driver_concrete: RTO-1's fan draws at most 3,800 scfm, and through 2026 the two fluid-bed dryers' drying cycles and a reactor's manway exhaust coincided often enough that the header carried more than the fan could draw in about 10,000 minutes; the excess lifted PSV-31 at the oxidizer inlet and left as untreated header gas, about 2,700 lb, so the tested 99.4 per cent applies only to what the fan drew.
stump: The default path applies RTO-1's tested 99.4 per cent destruction to every pound the batch records vent while the oxidizer was in RUN, counts its other minutes uncontrolled and files EU-P1 at 1.9 tons, under its 2.5-ton 2026 limit, because it never asks whether the oxidizer could draw every vent at once: when the dryers' drying cycles and a reactor's charging exhaust coincide the header carries more than RTO-1's 3,800 scfm, the excess lifts PSV-31 to atmosphere untreated, and EU-P1 emitted 3.2 tons.

differentiation.task106: task106 sizes each supplier against a whole pool of spare return legs that only one supplier can use, a static double-booking per corridor; here nothing is allocated between the vents: every vent's gas is real and reaches the header, and the step finds the minutes in which the vents' summed flow exceeded the oxidizer fan's instantaneous maximum, a coincidence in time that no per-source record or allocation shows.
differentiation.task303: task303 subtracts the breaker tickets every feeder at a substation opened in the same minute as one upstream supply loss; here the co-timed records are all genuine discharges and the step adds the share of them the shared device could not draw, so co-timing changes how much passed untreated, not whose event it was.
differentiation.task482: task482 architecture 7 reads a removal device whose outlet holds near a floor concentration, so its removal share falls as its inlet grows dilute; here the device's destruction is constant at its tested value and what fails is capture: the gas above the fan's maximum never reaches the device at all.
differentiation.task87: task87 caps a delivered count because two owed items meeting in one time slot cannot both be taken by one unit; here no unit chooses between items and nothing is deferred: the excess gas leaves through the relief the moment the header exceeds the draw.
differentiation.task472: task472 credits shortened work only where it reaches an earlier release window fixed outside the job; here no window is fixed by any schedule: the binding minutes are set by the coincidence of nine vents' own batch progress against one draw.
differentiation.task477: task477 re-times covered wages recorded in the period each payment is made onto the period earned, a calendar conformation of a published series ranked across industries; here nothing is re-timed or ranked: one unit's total is rebuilt from the minutes in which concurrent vents exceeded a fan's draw, and the gap shared on the cards (objective) and the generator G3 name a family, not a driver.
differentiation.task478: task478, the same pairing, carries a source test's emission rate across a burner's fuel where the rate rises with a fuel property a supplier reports, a per-unit factor problem across sources; here no factor is wrong or carried: the tested efficiency is right for what reached the oxidizer and the step is the share of the vents' coincident flow the fan could not draw.
differentiation.task480: task480, the same pairing, reads each unit's future amount from one cumulative total observed once at a past date, an increment over time; here the record is complete minute by minute and the step is the instantaneous sum across concurrent vents against one device's capacity.
differentiation.task310: task310 simulates an added store against recorded output censored by a send-out limit, an opportunity sized under a cap on what was recorded; here nothing is censored or simulated forward: every vent's step and rate is recorded and the cap is the fan's draw on the summed flow, which decides what left untreated in a closed year.

lineage.driver: A record of past events on units is carried to the units as they now stand, and some units were raised after their events, so a past event counts again on a raised unit only where the event's recorded level stood above the unit's new threshold; dropping a raised unit's earlier events, keeping them all, or giving it the later rate of units in its present class each misstates the expected rate.
